rationale:
bugs_open/352: the render audit records a class-less element's TAG NAME in a field called `Class`, so the orchestrator composes `H3.H3` / `p.P` / `A.A` — selectors no browser matches. css-patch-agent faithfully writes a rule against them, deploys it, and the work item completes honestly because a write really did happen. MEASURED 2026-08-24: of 452 `contrast_failure` rows, 181 carry a `TAG.TAG` selector and 108 of those are already `complete` — 108 recorded repairs that could never have applied. Actively producing: 92 filed in the last 7 days, first seen 2026-08-10.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE ONE-LINE FIX THE BUG FILE PROPOSES. 352 candidate (1) says to omit the class component so the selector reads `h3`. That is right about the producer and wrong about the consequence, and this is the whole reason for the design below. Today `p.P {color:#fff}` matches NOTHING, so it is inert and harmless. Corrected to `p` it matches — and css-patch-agent's own live prompt says "The platform APPENDS your rules to the END of the stylesheet", one stylesheet per site, so the rule recolours EVERY PARAGRAPH ON THE SITE. `P.P` (77) and `A.A` (44) are 121 of the 181: the two commonest cases are the two worst possible bare selectors. The naive fix converts a harmless no-op into a site-wide typography change on 13 sites. The lane that filed the bug has accepted this correction against its own candidate text.

SO THE INVARIANT IS NOT "STOP LYING", IT IS "PROVE IT". Every filed selector is composed IN THE PAGE and verified, in the same session that measured the failure, to select the very element measured (`Array.prototype.indexOf.call(document.querySelectorAll(sel), el) !== -1`), and carries its match count. A finding that fails that assertion, or whose selector is a bare tag, is COUNTED and reported, never filed and never silently dropped. Deleting the fallback fixes the one defect we found; the in-page assertion makes any future composition defect self-disclosing. That is the difference between "not produced" and "unrepresentable".

TWO HAZARDS THE OBVIOUS FIX CREATES, BOTH MEASURED, BOTH DESIGNED FOR.
(1) KEY SHAPE. `item_key` embeds the selector, and `retractResolvedContrastFindings` builds its still-failing set with the same composition. Change the producer and a legacy row keyed `#H3.H3` is absent from a new-shape set, its page WAS audited, so it is retracted as resolved and stamped "no longer below its contrast threshold" — FALSE, and the exact false completion that function's header says it exists to prevent. Exposure: 73 rows (58 `deferred` + 15 `unresolved`; `workItemClosedStatuses` excludes both) across 13 of 15 sites. This is not latent — the retraction path has ALREADY closed 79 contrast rows. Ordering cannot fix it: rekey first and the still-running OLD binary falsely retracts the rekeyed rows instead. The window is symmetric, so tolerance must live in the code.
(2) BLAST RADIUS, above.

WHAT MAKES EVERY DEPLOY ORDER INERT. The adapter KEEPS sending `class` with the fallback intact as a frozen legacy echo and adds `selector`/`matches`/`selector_verified` plus `summary.selector_scheme`. This matters because browser-runner-adapter and render-audit-adapter share one image (makefile:107-117) and roll SEPARATELY from agent-chassis, so all four skew cells are real: new-adapter/old-chassis is byte-identical to today (old chassis reads `class`, drops unknown keys); old-adapter/new-chassis falls back to `contrastSelector` for both filing and the still-failing set. Naively deleting `|| el.tagName` is precisely the version that opens the window — a new adapter against the old chassis emits bare `H3` keys and the OLD binary then falsely closes every legacy row on each audited page. Retraction additionally gains legacy ALIAS keys (both compositions inserted into still-failing, so a legacy row on a still-failing page can never read as resolved) and a scheme guard using the raw `Spec` already carried on `auditRetractionCandidate` for exactly this kind of judgement.

WHAT I AM DELIBERATELY NOT DOING. Arm 2 of 352 — a correct rule still losing on source order because the offending declaration sits in page-level component CSS emitted after the stylesheet the agent edits — is a different defect with a different remedy and stays OPEN with an arm banner on the bug file. I am not converging this probe on `contrast_check.go`'s `describe()` even though `describe` is the correct pattern and sits in the same package: it lowercases the tag and joins ALL class tokens, so adopting it would rekey EVERY CLASSED finding (`H2.card-title` -> `h2.card-title.muted`), turning a 73-row transition into a whole-population one for zero measurement benefit. Arm 1 of the composition is therefore byte-identical to today's `contrastSelector` output, which is what keeps the ~271 non-TAG.TAG rows completely undisturbed.

RFC_022 / optional-key-budget: not in scope and here is the enumeration rather than the assertion. No action config key is added — `WriteRenderAuditFindingsInputSpec` is untouched. The new fields are reply fields, opt-in BY PRESENCE with today's behaviour as the absent default, and the consumer set is exactly one action, `write_render_audit_findings`, which is the only reader of `renderAuditPayload`.

plan.summary: Make an unmatchable CSS selector unrepresentable at the producer rather than merely un-emitted: compose the selector in-page (class -> own id -> nearest ancestor anchor -> bare tag), assert it selects the element that was just measured, and carry `matches` + `selector_verified` + `summary.selector_scheme` as ADDITIVE reply fields while the legacy `class` echo stays byte-identical so every adapter/chassis skew order is inert. The filer prefers the verified selector, falls back to today's `contrastSelector` when absent, and REFUSES two categories with their own counters: unverified (`skipped_unverified_selector`) and unanchored bare-tag (`skipped_unanchored_selector`, which also closes a live hazard — a whitespace-only className already files a bare-tag selector today). Retraction gains legacy alias keys and a scheme guard so no key-shape change can falsely close a live row, and its reason string is reworded to stop over-claiming about the element when only the selector pairing was observed. Migration 586 (_HOLD) WITHDRAWS the 73 open invented-selector rows as `cancelled` — withdrawal, not resolution — freeing the dedup slot so the next weekly audit re-files the still-failing ones under verified selectors.

edits.rationale: The producer half of the invariant, and the only place where the truth is available: the page is open in Chromium, so the selector can be verified against the element that was measured. Fields are ADDITIVE and the `class` echo keeps the fallback verbatim — that echo is the skew keel, not timidity, because it is what makes new-adapter/old-chassis byte-identical to today. Composition arm 1 reproduces today's `contrastSelector` output byte-for-byte so the ~271 classed rows keep their item_key.

This test byte-pins auditJS to testdata/audit_js_golden_2026-08-22.txt AND pins that golden's sha256 to a digest taken from b32aa9cd9~1 — i.e. from a commit OTHER than the one under review — precisely so 'a golden silently regenerated from the post-refactor code' cannot prove the change against itself. Repointing it at a new golden with a new sha would DISCARD that property, because both artefacts would then come from my own code, and two artefacts from one source are one artefact. So the guarantee changes shape from IDENTITY to CONFINEMENT and the historical digest stays.

Three tests, each failing on a distinct mutation. The copy-through test fails if the fields or the unconditional scheme stamp regress; the counter test fails if an unverified finding is dropped without being counted (the no-silent-caps half); the env-gated Chromium test is the ONLY one that executes the JS and is what fails if the tag fallback ever reaches the selector again. Stating plainly that it is gated: the golden confinement pin is the ungated backstop.

The reason string is reworded because it asserts something about the ELEMENT when only the SELECTOR PAIRING was observed. `renderAuditContrast` is a hand-kept MIRROR of ContrastFinding (platform/ must not import internal/adapters), so missing it would make the field unmarshal into nothing and read as absent with no error.

Each names the mutation it catches. The paired retraction control exists so the alias guard cannot be 'satisfied' by never retracting at all — a guard that blocks everything is a silent false BLOCK, which is the same defect wearing the other sign.

UnverifiedSelectorIsSkippedAndCounted  — empty tx + counter; deleting the guard yields an unexpected INSERT

edits.rationale: The 73 open rows cannot be truthfully rekeyed: the correct new key is DOM-derived (the ancestor anchor), which SQL cannot compute, and a bare-tag rekey would hand a parked fixer exactly the site-wide selector this change exists to refuse. `cancelled` asserts WITHDRAWAL, not resolution; it is in workItemClosedStatuses so no retraction can ever touch these rows again; and by migration 157 it frees the dedup slot so the next weekly audit re-files the still-failing ones under verified selectors. I originally argued for rekeying to preserve the two-strike attempt count — that argument is DEAD: the counter reads only complete/failed within 7 days (load_work_item_actions.go:1519-1523) and the park dates from 2026-08-11, so there is no history to preserve, and the attempts spent were aimed at a selector that could never match.

Withdrawn, not resolved: a still-failing pairing is re-filed with an in-page-verified selector by the next weekly render audit.')

plan.risks: 1) FIRST OBJECTION, EXPECTED FROM THE GUARDIAN SEAT: a migration closes 73 findings inside a bug fix. Answer: `cancelled` asserts withdrawal not resolution; each row's selector provably matches nothing, which IS the bug and is measurable rather than argued; re-detection is automatic and weekly; the prior status is preserved in result.pre_352_status with a NOT EXISTS-guarded rollback; and the alternative is a standing population of parked rows whose specs aim fixers at impossible selectors — which is what the brochure lane was about to release. 2) ANCHOR CHURN: a renamed section class re-keys a class-less finding, so the old anchored row retracts (with the reworded, still-true reason) while the successor files in the same transaction. State converges to one correct open row; a reviewer may fairly call the interim reason weak, and the rewording is the mitigation rather than a cure. 3) THE JS IS UNTESTABLE UNGATED — the behavioural test needs BROWSER_RUNNER_IT=1 and real Chromium; the golden CONFINEMENT pin is the review-time guard. Named plainly rather than papered over. 4) KEEPING THE LYING `class` FIELD is deliberate (the skew keel) and is the part most likely to be mistaken for an oversight by a later reader — hence the inline comment naming it and the retirement condition recorded in the bug file. 5) `skipped_unanchored_selector` withholds real failures from the fixer. It is COUNTED, not silent, but a reviewer should push on whether an unanchored finding deserves its own item type rather than a skip; my answer is that it does, and that inventing one here would be the same over-reach as folding in arm 2. 6) I have NOT established that the locked-component substring check ever dropped a real finding — 6 sites with locked components hold 108 contrast items of which 51 ARE TAG.TAG, so the mechanism permits the drop and the evidence does not show it happening. Stated as permitted-not-observed, and the anchoring change narrows rather than provably closes it.
